office_does: The county clerk is clerk of the Superior Court: the office keeps court files and records, takes filings and fees and manages the jury pool; four-year term.
race_blurb: Democrat Grace D. Cross, clerk for ten years, faces Republican Olivia D. Munsch, a 14-year employee of the same office; the primary was 2,153 to 2,098. Both promise accessible, accurate service: Cross cites e-filing and online records, Munsch published fee schedules, plain-language help and jury-service outreach to employers.

candidates.summary: Skamania County Clerk for ten years after a decade on the office's staff; running for re-election as a Democrat.
highlights: Added e-filing, online public records and electronic jury summons responses [S1][S2]
Prioritizes staff training and technology for consistent service [S2]
Raised $8,429 by Sept. 30, including $1,500 from the county Democratic Party [S5][S6]

experience.basis: Twenty years in the Clerk's Office, ten as the elected clerk, re-elected unopposed in 2022, running on her record of modernizing the office.

candidates.summary: Lifetime county resident from Carson with 18 years in county employment, 14 in the Clerk's Office; running as a Republican on her first campaign.
highlights: Would publish policies, fee schedules and court information online and in print [S2]
Proposes a patron feedback system and jury-service education for employers [S2]
Raised $7,529 by Sept. 27, about half of it her own money [S4][S5]

experience.basis: A challenger on her first run, but a 14-year staff member of the office she seeks who runs on that experience and continuity of service, not on outsider change.
